dialogs.title: บทสนทนา — Monday morning, talking about Chiang Mai
dialogs.intro: Budi has just come back from his trip. The last dialogue of this module is long on purpose: almost every pattern from the twenty units appears in it. Read it once without looking at the translation, and see how much you understand on your own.

lines.speaker: นก:
lines.text: [พี่|Phîi][บูดี|Buu-dii] [กลับ|klàp][มา|maa][แล้ว|láaeo][เหรอ|rǒoe][คะ|khá] [เชียงใหม่|Chiang-mài][เป็น|pen][ยังไง|yang-ngai][บ้าง|bâang][คะ|khá]
lines.id: Phi Budi, you're back? How was Chiang Mai?
lines.literal: older-sibling — Budi — return — come — already — huh — (polite)? Chiang-Mai — be — how — some — (polite)?

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [สนุก|Sà-nùk][มาก|mâak][ครับ|khráp] [แต่|Tàae][เหนื่อย|nùueai][เหมือนกัน|mǔuean-kan][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: So much fun. But tiring too.

lines.speaker: นก:
lines.text: [ไป|Pai][กี่|kìi][วัน|wan][คะ|khá] [ทำ|Tham][อะไร|à-rai][บ้าง|bâang][คะ|khá]
lines.id: How many days did you go for? What did you do?
lines.literal: go — how-many — day — (polite)? do — what — some — (polite)?

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [สาม|Sǎam][วัน|wan][ครับ|khráp] [ตอนแรก|Tawn-râaek][ไป|pai][วัด|wát][ครับ|khráp] [แล้ว|Láaeo][ก็|kâw][ไป|pai][ตลาด|tà-làat][กลางคืน|klaang-khuuen][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: Three days. First I went to a temple. Then to the night market.
lines.literal: three — day — (polite). at-first — go — temple — (polite). then — also — go — market — night — (polite).

lines.speaker: นก:
lines.text: [ไป|Pai][ดอย|dawy][สุเทพ|Sù-thêep][ไหม|mǎi][คะ|khá]
lines.id: Did you go to Doi Suthep?

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ไป|Pai][ครับ|khráp] [วัน|Wan][ที่|thîi][สอง|sǎawng][ครับ|khráp] [ต้อง|Tâwng][เดิน|dooen][ขึ้น|khûen][บันได|ban-dai][เยอะ|yóe][มาก|mâak][ครับ|khráp] [เกือบ|Kùueap][ไม่|mâi][ไหว|wǎi][ครับ|khráp]

lines.literal: go — (polite). day — the — two — (polite). must — walk — up — stairs — many — very — (polite). almost — not — able — (polite).

lines.speaker: นก:
lines.text: [ฮ่าๆ|Hâa-hâa] [แต่|tàae][วิว|wiu][สวย|sǔai][ที่สุด|thîi-sùt][ใช่|châi][ไหม|mǎi][คะ|khá]
lines.id: Haha, but the view was the best, right?
lines.literal: haha — but — view — beautiful — most — correct — (question) — (polite)?

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [สวย|Sǔai][จริงๆ|jing-jing][ครับ|khráp] [ประทับใจ|Prà-tháp-jai][มาก|mâak][ครับ|khráp] [หลังจากนั้น|Lǎng-jàak-nán][ไป|pai][กิน|kin][ข้าวซอย|khâao-sawy][ครับ|khráp] [อร่อย|À-ràwy][ที่สุด|thîi-sùt][เท่าที่|thâo-thîi][เคย|khoei][กิน|kin][มา|maa][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: It was really beautiful. Very moving. After that I had khao soi. The best I've ever eaten.
lines.literal: beautiful — truly — (polite). impressed-heart — very — (polite). after-that — go — eat — khao-soi — (polite). tasty — most — as-far-as — ever — eat — come — (polite).

lines.speaker: นก:
lines.text: [ข้าวซอย|Khâao-sawy][เผ็ด|phèt][ไหม|mǎi][คะ|khá] [พี่|Phîi][กิน|kin][เผ็ด|phèt][ไม่ค่อย|mâi-khâwy][ได้|dâai][นี่|nîi][คะ|khá]
lines.id: Was the khao soi spicy? You can't really handle spicy food, can you?
lines.literal: khao-soi — spicy — (question) — (polite)? older-sibling — eat — spicy — not-very — can — you-know — (polite)?

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ผม|Phǒm][บอก|bàwk][เขา|khǎo][ว่า|wâa][ไม่|mâi][เผ็ด|phèt][ครับ|khráp] [แล้ว|Láaeo][ก็|kâw][ขอ|khǎaw][ไม่|mâi][ใส่|sài][หมู|mǔu][ด้วย|dûai][ครับ|khráp] [เขา|Khǎo][เข้าใจ|khâo-jai][เลย|loei][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: I told them not spicy. And I asked for no pork too. They understood right away.
lines.literal: I — tell — them — that — not — spicy — (polite). then — also — ask — not — put — pork — too — (polite). they — understand — straight-away — (polite).

lines.speaker: นก:
lines.text: [เก่ง|Kèng][แล้ว|láaeo][นะ|ná][คะ|khá] [ภาษาไทย|Phaa-sǎa-thai][ดีขึ้น|dii-khûen][เยอะ|yóe][เลย|loei][ค่ะ|khâ]
lines.id: You're getting good. Your Thai has improved a lot.
lines.literal: clever — already — huh — (polite). Thai-language — improve — a-lot — really — (polite).

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ขอบคุณ|Khàwp-khun][ครับ|khráp] [ยัง|Yang][ต้อง|tâwng][เรียน|rian][อีก|ìik][เยอะ|yóe][ครับ|khráp] [แต่|Tàae][ตอนนี้|tawn-níi][พูด|phûut][กับ|kàp][คน|khon][ไทย|thai][ได้|dâai][แล้ว|láaeo][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: Thanks. I still have a lot to learn. But now I can talk with Thai people.
lines.literal: thank-you — (polite). still — must — learn — more — a-lot — (polite). but — now — talk — with — people — Thai — can — already — (polite).

lines.speaker: นก:
lines.text: [คราวหน้า|Khraao-nâa][ไป|pai][ด้วย|dûai][กัน|kan][นะ|ná][คะ|khá] [จะ|Jà][พา|phaa][ไป|pai][ร้าน|ráan][ที่|thîi][คน|khon][ไทย|thai][ไป|pai][กัน|kan][ค่ะ|khâ]
lines.id: Let's go together next time. I'll take you to the places Thai people go.
lines.literal: next-time — go — with — together — okay — (polite). will — take — go — shop — that — people — Thai — go — together — (polite).

lines.speaker: บูดี:
lines.text: [ดี|Dii][เลย|loei][ครับ|khráp] [ขอบคุณ|Khàwp-khun][มาก|mâak][นะ|ná][ครับ|khráp] [แล้ว|Láaeo][เจอ|joee][กัน|kan][ครับ|khráp]
lines.id: I'd love that. Thank you so much. See you later.
lines.literal: good — really — (polite). thank-you — much — okay — (polite). then — meet — together — (polite).

notes: **บ้าง bâang at the end of a question means "what all, which ones" — asking for several answers, not one.** *ทำอะไรบ้าง* (what did you get up to?), *ไปที่ไหนบ้าง* (where all did you go?), *เป็นยังไงบ้าง* (how did it all go?). Without *บ้าง*, the question expects a single answer. This little word instantly makes your questions sound natural.
**เป็นยังไงบ้าง pen yang-ngai bâang = "how was it?"**, the standard opener for asking for a story: about a trip, work, health, anything. The answer can be as short as one adjective: *สนุกมากครับ*.

**A story is built with four linking words you already know:** *ตอนแรก tawn-râaek* (at first), *แล้วก็ láaeo-kâw* (then), *หลังจากนั้น lǎng-jàak-nán* (after that), *สุดท้าย sùt-tháai* (finally). With these four you can tell anything in order without a single verb changing form.
**เท่าที่เคย…มา thâo-thîi khoei … maa = "that I've ever…".** *อร่อยที่สุดเท่าที่เคยกินมา* = the tastiest I've ever eaten. This pattern sounds mature and is often used to share impressions.

**ประทับใจ prà-tháp-jai = "impressed, moved", literally "stamped on the heart".** One more member of the *ใจ* family from unit 19. It's the right word for describing a meaningful experience, deeper than *สนุก*.
**เกือบ kùueap = "almost".** *เกือบไม่ไหว* (almost didn't make it), *เกือบลืม* (almost forgot), *เกือบสาย* (almost late). You'll hear it constantly in everyday conversation.

**นี่ nîi at the end of a sentence means "you know, after all" — pointing to something both people already know.** *พี่กินเผ็ดไม่ค่อยได้นี่คะ* = "you can't really handle spicy food, can you". It differs from the *นี่* that means "this"; position tells them apart.

**ข้าวซอย khâao-sawy is Chiang Mai's signature dish** — coconut curry noodles topped with crispy fried noodles. It's one of the best-known dishes of northern Thailand, and usually not as spicy as Isan food.

after: **Notice the ไป…มา *pai … maa*** pattern you've seen since unit 11: it means "went there and came back". *ผมไปเชียงใหม่มาครับ* is the most natural way to say "I've just been to Chiang Mai" — far more natural than using *แล้ว*.

A complete example story, using only words you already have: *อาทิตย์ที่แล้วผมไปเชียงใหม่มาครับ ไปกับเพื่อนสามคน ตอนแรกไปวัด แล้วก็ไปตลาดกลางคืน หลังจากนั้นไปกินข้าวซอย สุดท้ายกลับกรุงเทพฯ วันอาทิตย์ครับ สนุกมากครับ คราวหน้าจะไปอีกครับ*

grammars.title: Responding to someone's story
body: Responding well matters as much as telling the story. In Thailand, a warm response is valued far more than a long one.

head: Thai
Pronunciation
Meaning
rows: เหนื่อยไหม
แล้วยังไงต่อ
เสียดายจัง
ดีใจด้วยนะ
ครั้งหน้าไปด้วยกันนะ

after: ⚠️ **เสียดาย *sǐa-daai* — "what a shame" — is different from เสียใจ *sǐa-jai* (sad).** The first is for a missed chance: *เสียดายที่ไปไม่ได้* (too bad I couldn't go). The second is for real sadness or condolences.

sections.title: Impressions and feelings after the fact

blocks.title: Three ways to end a story
items: **คุ้มมากครับ/ค่ะ** — totally worth it. The best closing line for a trip that was tiring but memorable.
**คราวหน้าจะไปอีกครับ/ค่ะ** — next time I want to go again.
**ไว้เล่าให้ฟังนะครับ/คะ** *wái lâo hâi fang ná* — I'll tell you more later. Used when you're out of time but the story isn't finished.

sections.title: You've made it this far — what next

blocks.text: If you've worked through all twenty units of this module, you now hold the entire framework of everyday Thai. Not part of it: **all of it**. Five tones, sentence patterns that never change, classifiers, time markers, verb helpers, comparisons, and how to keep the atmosphere pleasant.
All you're missing are two things: **a wider vocabulary** and **hours of practice**. No book can give you either. Both come from using the language.

blocks.title: Four things that will boost your skills fastest now
items: **Repeat the dialogues of units 1 to 20 out loud, one unit a day.** Twenty days, twenty minutes a day. This is the repetition that turns "I understood it once" into "it comes out on its own".

**Start reading the script.** You've seen Thai script thousands of times in this module. Take the table in the opening chapter, memorize the nine middle-class consonants, then start sounding out signs and menus. From there, vocabulary comes in through your eyes, not just your ears.
**Speak sooner than feels comfortable.** A missed tone is almost always guessed from context. What can't be guessed is the sentence you never say.
**Find one Thai person to talk with regularly** — a coworker, a favorite vendor, a neighbor. One short conversation every day beats three hours of study once a week.

blocks.text: And one last thing, already mentioned in unit 19 and worth repeating on the final page: **your tones may slip, your manner mustn't.** A messy sentence said with a smile, ending in *ครับ* or *ค่ะ*, will take you much further than perfect grammar delivered in a rush.
*ขอบคุณที่เรียนจนจบนะครับ/คะ โชคดีครับ/ค่ะ* — thank you for studying all the way to the end. Good luck.
